analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. The changed hunk, at head lines ~2115-2131, is outside the two supplied head excerpts (lines 1-451 and 452-927). That hunk adds documentation for running python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/models for the Model Requant Upload workflow. It describes the tests as network-free and credential-free, using a fake aws and python3, a secret-free preflight, a prod-environment upload job, master-only gating, a check of both R2 key sets that prints only pass or fail, tools pinned by hash, and a selftest run before any secret is used. I examined the supplied excerpts, which are unchanged context. They contain test instructions, isolated state guidance, and warnings never to use production cache roots or keys, none of which were modified. No runtime code, authorization, attestation, encryption, or cache-storage behavior changes, so no threat-model assets, boundaries, or mitigations (e.g. T-041, TB-007, A-001) are affected. The documented workflow controls (prod environment, master-only, hash-pinned tools, check before upload) describe the model-publication path, which is platform and CI scoped. I could not verify those claims against the real workflow or scripts/models source, since neither was supplied. A later pass could confirm the documented controls match the workflow, but this documentation-only change creates no concrete security regression.
